title: Descent of punctual purity along proper invertible-degree maps
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Use punctual purity of regular Noetherian schemes with $\ell$ invertible as in [def-per-punctual-purity], with regularity as in [def-weil-regular-scheme] and the canonical Kummer classes of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait here is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a discrete valuation ring: a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal. A complete strictly henselian trait has $R$ complete for its maximal-ideal topology and henselian with separably closed residue field (henselian means that every simple root over the residue field of a monic polynomial over $R$ lifts to a root over $R$). Mixed characteristic means that $\operatorname{Frac}R$ has characteristic zero and the residue field has positive characteristic.

Let $S$ be a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $f:V\to W$ be a proper dominant $S$-morphism of integral regular schemes of finite type and quasi-projective over $S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over $S$. Suppose that $f$ is generically finite etale of positive degree $d$ not divisible by $\ell$, meaning finite etale of degree $d$ over a nonempty open subscheme of $W$. If $V$ is punctually pure, then $W$ is punctually pure. No flatness hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.5.7 and proof, Lemmas 3.5.8--3.5.10, printed pp.249--250: the Gysin comparison is a retract of its proper direct image since the two degree composites are multiplication by d. Restricted to the complete mixed-characteristic traits used in section 3.7.

proof.text: For $T=V,W$, put $e_T=\operatorname{vdim}(T/S)$ and $K_T=p_T^!A_S(-e_T)[-2e_T]$. The prepurity lci calculus supplies $c_T:A_T\to K_T$. Because $f$ is dominant generically finite etale, $e_V=e_W$ and $f^!K_W\cong K_V$. Write $g:A_V\to f^!A_W$ for its virtual-dimension-zero class. The composition formula gives $c_V=f^!(c_W)g$. The relative-class criterion applied to the hypothesized punctual purity of $V$ says that $c_V$ is an isomorphism. Both schemes satisfy its integral, regular, finite-type and quasi-projective hypotheses, over the same complete strictly henselian trait.

source.place: XVI, Proposition 3.5.7 proof, using Proposition 3.5.5 and Theorem 2.5.12.

proof.text:
Properness gives $Rf_!=Rf_*$ by the identity-open compactification. Transpose $g$ under $Rf_*\dashv f^!$ to obtain $t:Rf_*A_V\to A_W$. For $M\in D^+(W_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ define
$$T_M:Rf_*f^*M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}M\otimes^LRf_*A_V\xrightarrow{1\otimes t}M.$$
The proper projection formula makes the first arrow invertible; all coefficients are finite and all schemes Noetherian. Its $Rf_*\dashv f^!$ transpose is $a_M:f^*M\to f^!M$. Naturality of tensor, projection and adjunction gives $f^!(b)a_M=a_Nf^*(b)$ for every $b:M\to N$. With the unit object, $T_{A_W}=t$ and $a_{A_W}=g$, by the definition of the transpose.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 3.5.8 proof; the proper specialization of its tensor/projection construction.

proof.text:
Let $u_M:M\to Rf_*f^*M$ be the ordinary inverse-image unit and $\epsilon_M:Rf_*f^!M\to M$ the exceptional counit. Set $H=Rf_*c_V$, $i_A=u_{A_W}$, $r_A=t$, $i_K=Rf_*a_{K_W}\,u_{K_W}$ and $r_K=\epsilon_{K_W}$, identifying $f^!K_W=K_V$. Naturality of $a$ at $c_W$ and of $u$ gives
$$H i_A=i_Kc_W.$$
Indeed $a_{K_W}f^*c_W=f^!c_Wg=c_V$. Naturality of $\epsilon$ gives
$$r_KH=\epsilon_{K_W}Rf_*(f^!c_Wg)=c_W\epsilon_{A_W}Rf_*g=c_Wr_A.$$
Thus $c_W$ is connected to $H$ by a morphism of arrows in each direction. These equations use only naturality and the composition identity established in step 1.

source.place: XVI, the two commutative diagrams in the proof of Proposition 3.5.7, printed pp.249--250.

proof.text: Choose the nonempty open $j:U\hookrightarrow W$ in the hypothesis, where $f_U:f^{-1}U\to U$ is finite etale of degree $d$. Open exchange for compact supports, its paired right-adjoint restriction, and compatibility of projection maps with restriction identify the restrictions of $T_M,u_M,\epsilon_M$ with those for $f_U$. The classes restrict by the prepurity lci calculus. The finite-etale ambidexterity statement therefore identifies both restricted composites $j^*(r_Ai_A)$ and $j^*(r_Ki_K)$ with multiplication by $d$, the latter for the complex $j^*K_W$. This is a derived-category identity for the actual counits, rather than a claim that arbitrary derived morphisms can be tested on stalk maps.

source.place: XVI, Lemmas 3.5.9--3.5.10, reduction to a nonempty finite-etale open and its adjunction calculation.

proof.text:
The scheme $W$ is integral, hence nonempty and connected, and so is $U$. Since $A_W$ is concentrated in degree zero,
$$\operatorname{End}_{D^+(W_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(A_W)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}_A}(A_W,A_W)=\Gamma(W,A_W)=A.$$
The last equality holds because a locally constant function from a connected scheme to the finite discrete set $A$ is constant. Its restriction to $U$ is the identity on $A$. Consequently step 4 gives $r_Ai_A=d\operatorname{id}_{A_W}$. The scalar-restriction lemma applies to $K_W$ without assuming purity of $W$; its restriction is injective, and step 4 gives $r_Ki_K=d\operatorname{id}_{K_W}$. No statement about the scalar endomorphisms of the constant sheaf is being used to assert scalar endomorphisms of an arbitrary complex.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 3.5.9 proof, printed p.250, scalar detection for the two endomorphisms.

proof.text:
Since $\ell\nmid d$, multiplication by $d$ is a unit of $A=\mathbf F_\ell$; write its inverse as $b$. The map $H=Rf_*c_V$ is invertible because $c_V$ is, and functors preserve inverses. Define $h=b\,r_AH^{-1}i_K:K_W\to A_W$. The equations of steps 3 and 5 imply
$$hc_W=b\,r_AH^{-1}Hi_A=b\,r_Ai_A=1,$$
$$c_Wh=b\,r_KHH^{-1}i_K=b\,r_Ki_K=1.$$
Thus $c_W$ is an isomorphism, with the displayed explicit inverse. This is the retract computation; it needs neither an abstract idempotent-completeness theorem nor a flatness hypothesis on $f$.

source.place: XVI, Proposition 3.5.7 proof after the second diagram, and Lemma 3.5.9.

proof.text: Apply the reverse implication of the relative-class criterion to $W$. Invertibility of $c_W$ implies that, for every $w\in W$, the localized Kummer map $A_{\kappa(w)}\to j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$ is an isomorphism. This is precisely the definition of punctual purity in the item, so $W$ is punctually pure.

source.place: XVI, Proposition 3.5.5 applied at the end of Proposition 3.5.7.

proof_origin.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.5.7, Lemmas 3.5.8--3.5.10, printed pp.249--250.

statement_change.what: The statement introduced punctual purity inline although def-per-punctual-purity already owns ILO XVI 3.2.1--3.2.2. Its delivered Yoneda helpers duplicated the same transpose-isomorphism notion with a non-definitional predicate, preventing direct composition with other punctual-purity results. Replace the inline definition by a reference to the existing definition node, add that statement dependency, and use its IsPunctuallyPure predicate. No geometric hypothesis or mathematical purity condition changes.
